Draft research pass (research_makedonya.json): Kănčov-based placement of Turks, Pomaks, Torbeş, Albanians and Vallahades; Shaw & Shaw vol. 2 p.208; EB 1911 'Macedonia'. Retained as cross-checks only.
caveats: Baseline year: the only complete Ottoman count by kaza is the 1881/82 census, which was enumerated in Macedonia in 1881-84. It is used as the 1876 baseline. It already contains Muslim muhacirs who arrived in 1877-81 from Bulgaria, Serbia (the Niš/Toplica Albanians in Üsküp and Kumanova) and Thessaly. It also lacks Bulgarians who fled after the 1878 Kresna-Razlog rising. Both effects make the Muslim shares the upper end of what an Ottoman source supports for 1876, as the source policy asks. The pre-war register counts in the Ethnographie (1878) are lower for most kazas; for example Nevrekop 43% Muslim, Petriç 27%, Manastır sancağı 15-20% (males).

The 1885 Selanik salname figure (494,656 Muslims, 49.6% without Katerin) is higher than the census (45.3%). It was not applied because it has no kaza breakdown and it follows the 1881 Thessaly cession and the Muslim refugee wave into Selanik. Applying it pro rata would add about 40,000 Muslims to the Selanik vilayet clusters.

Female under-registration was corrected for every group by raising female counts to the male count (M + max(F,M)), which is the 'male count x 2' rule. In this census Christian women were under-registered slightly more than Muslim women (F/M: Muslims 0.94, Greeks 0.87, Bulgarians 0.88). The correction therefore lowers the Selanik vilayet Muslim share by about 0.8 points against the raw census. No further Muslim-only uplift was made, because no Turkish or Ottoman source gives a figure for unregistered Yörüks or Circassians in Macedonia in 1876. Circassians in Macedonia arrived after 1878.
Kalkandelen: Karpat notes that Prizren sancağı was counted largely without females, so the 44,032 were doubled to 88,064. The 1894 Kosova figures and Kănčov's 79,509 (1900) are consistent with this.

Debre-i Bala and Rekalar were not in the 1881/82 census. The total is the Ethnographie male count doubled (71,656) minus about 6,000 for Golo Brdo, which is left to the Albania dataset. The cluster shares were kept from the draft (Kănčov-based, 57% Muslim). That is higher than the register-based Ethnographie (48.5%) and follows Karpat's note that Debre registration was incomplete. Confidence is low to medium.

Nevrekop: in the 1881/82 count and the 1303 salname, the kaza included the Tamraş Pomak villages, which in 1876 belonged to Filibe sancağı and are covered by the Edirne dataset. About 8,800 Muslims were removed; this is Kănčov's difference between the 1303 salname and his own count, so it is an approximate figure. Kănčov's village table was then used only to place the Ottoman totals.

Intra-kaza populations are estimates. Town sizes follow the order of magnitude in the salnames and Kănčov, and the rest of the kaza is spread over the rural clusters. Only the kaza sums are source-based. Cluster Muslim shares were fitted by a uniform logit shift of the draft's (Kănčov-based) pattern so that each kaza matches the census Muslim total. Fixed exceptions: Selanik city (salname 62% Muslim), Cuma-i Bala town and Simitli Pomaks, the five Nevrekop clusters, and Aynaroz.

Turk vs other Muslim: no Ottoman source separates them. The split follows the draft's language placement. Kocacık, Ovçepole, Radovişte and Koçana Yörüks, Konyars of Kayalar and Kozana, Župa Turks, Gostivar and Tetovo Turkish-speaking townsmen and Tikveş 'Türklük' villages are counted as turk. Pomaks, Torbeş, Albanians, Vallahades, Meglen Pomaks, Muslim Megleno-Romanians and Muslim Roma are counted as muslim_other. Result: Turks are about 74% of Muslims in Selanik vilayet, 62% in the Manastır part and 48% in the Prizren part. Region total: 27.5% Turk, 14.9% other Muslim, 57.6% Christian, 1,972,110 people.

Calibration: the clusters inside modern Blagoevgrad oblast (Petriç, Menlik, Cuma-i Bala, Razlık and the Bulgarian part of Nevrekop; 167,488 people) give about 50.7% Bulgarians. This counts Melnik's 2,699 Rum and half of the small Rum counts in Cuma and Nevrekop as non-Bulgarian. The target is 55%: the result is inside the ±5 band but near its lower edge, because the 1881/82 Muslim shares are used. Using the pre-war Ethnographie register counts for Petriç, Menlik and Nevrekop instead would raise it to about 55-57%. No other target oblast lies in this region; Kyustendil and Dupnitsa belong to the Tuna/Sofya dataset.

Uncertain kaza assignments: Karacaova (Meglen) is split between Yenice (east) and Vodina (west), following the Ethnographie's Vodina village list and Kănčov's Yenice figure. Paiko-Gümendze and Nânta-Ljumnica are placed in Gevgili. Pravişte is inside Drama kaza, as the 1881/82 totals imply. The Pangeon Greek villages are placed in Zihne. Kruševo, Resne-Prespa, Bigla-Demirhisar and Mariovo are placed in Manastır kaza; the 1880 sancak list has Prespa, Resne and Mariovo as müdürlüks, and Kănčov lists Kruševo under Bitola. Maleş (Pehčevo-Berovo) is in Koçana, as the 1881 totals imply. Poreče is in Kırçova and Sorovic-Ekşisu is in Lerin. Kocacık-Lahna is placed in Avrethisar.

Administrative status in 1876: Selanik vilayeti (Selanik, Serez and Drama sancakları); Manastır vilayeti, 1874-77 (Manastır sancağı, Görice sancağı with Kesriye, Serfice sancağı); Prizren vilayeti, 1871-77 (Üsküp sancağı, Prizren sancağı with Kalkandelen, Debre sancağı). Köprülü, Tikveş, Usturumca, Doyran and Gevgili were in Selanik sancağı. Sources differ on when Serfice was attached to Manastır and on whether Kalkandelen belonged to Prizren or Üsküp sancağı.

Overlaps were removed: the Görice/Korçë cluster and Golo Brdo are left to the Albania/Yanya dataset, which covers Görice sancağı except Kesriye. Alasonya is left to the Thessaly dataset. Tamraş is left to the Edirne dataset. Taşoz (Thasos), an Egyptian khedival domain with a Greek population, is not covered because no Ottoman count was found; it will appear empty on the map.
Jews (Selanik about 35,000-39,500; Manastır, Serez, Kesriye, Karaferye, Kavala, Üsküp) are excluded and shares renormalised. Selanik's Dönme are counted as Turks.
changes: Method for all kazas: Muslim and non-Muslim kaza totals are now the Ottoman 1881/82 census figures (Karpat 1985, Table I.8.A), with females corrected to the male count. They replace the draft's 'Kănčov +2-4 points' baseline. The draft's spatial pattern inside each kaza is kept and shifted to match the census.

Selanik city: Muslim share raised from 52% to 62% (turk 57, other 5), from the salname figures in Tepekaya/Gökbilgin (24,528 Muslims against 11,706 Rum and 1,111 Bulgarians). Selanik kaza as a whole: 42.8% Muslim (census 30,372 of 71,046).

Kaza Muslim shares raised to the census values (draft → new, same populations): Langaza 41→58%, Avrethisar/Kukuş 42→57%, Toyran 65→71%, Usturumca 38→48%, Gevgili 33→43%, Yenice-i Vardar 47→53%, Vodina 39→45%, Tikveş 43→47%, Köprülü 28→35%, Kesendire 9→13%. Turkish Yörük and plain villages (Kocacık, Avrethisar plain, Langaza basin, Valandova, Strumica plain) now reach 65-88% Turk.

Serez sancağı raised: Serez kaza 30→38% Muslim (Serez city 57%), Zihne 16→22%, Demirhisar 33→39%, Petriç 32→36%, Menlik 22→36%, Razlık 28→39%. Cuma-i Bala lowered 34→27.5%, because the census figure (6,218 of 22,646) matches Kănčov exactly and is lower than the draft's allocation.

Nevrekop rebuilt: 1881/82 totals minus about 8,800 Tamraş Pomaks (Filibe sancağı in 1876; Kănčov's note on the 1303 salname), giving 82,262 people, 60.3% Muslim. The draft's 'Nevrekop güneyi' cluster was split into Hacıdimova–Mesta (Bulgaria, 94% Christian) and Zırnova–Kato Nevrokopi (Greece, 33% Muslim, Turkish villages). Çeç was enlarged to 27,214 people (97% Muslim).
Drama sancağı raised: Drama kaza 69→75% Muslim (Drama town 76%, Pravişte plain 78%), Kavala 82→86%, Sarışaban 92→95% (census 16,554 Muslims of 17,388).

Üsküp sancağı raised: Üsküp kaza 50→58% Muslim (city 64→74%), Kumanova 26→28%, Koçana (with Maleş) 37→40%, İştip 54→57%, Radovişte 58→60%. Kratova stays at 18%. Eğri Palanka is lowered 12→10% to the census.

Kalkandelen raised 60→66% Muslim, based on the male-only census figure (29,212 Muslims of 44,032) doubled to 88,064 people. Turkish-speaking townsmen are kept as turk in Tetovo (45%) and Gostivar–Vrapčište (32%).

Serfice sancağı raised: Kayalar (Cuma) 67→77% Muslim (Konyar core 88% Turk), Kozana 52→53% (Konyar plain 89% Turk), Serfice 19→25%, Nasliç 21→24%. Grebene is lowered 16→14% to the census (4,940 Muslims of 34,978).

Manastır sancağı lowered where the Ottoman count is lower: Manastır kaza 28→22% Muslim (census 30,517 of 137,049; Bitola city 52→43%), Pirlepe 25→23%. Raised slightly: Lerin 27→29%, Ohri 30→32%, Kırçova 38→39%, Kesriye 18→22%. Katerin is lowered 19→15% to the census (3,944 Muslims of 25,772).

Debre-i Bala and Rekalar: the draft shares (57% Muslim) are kept rather than lowered to the Ethnographie register value (48.5%), because Karpat reports Debre as not censused and the registers as incomplete. The Debre town cluster was renamed and enlarged (r 7 km, 20,000 people) to include the Debar plain.

Tikveş split kept at about 1 Turk to 2 Slavic-speaking Muslims, following TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi 'Tikveş': Yörük 'Türklük' villages and Turkish-speaking townsmen as turk, western-Tikveş converts as muslim_other.

Coverage changes: removed Görice/Korçë and Golo Brdo (Albania dataset). Split Karacaova into Yenice and Vodina parts. Added 'Kukuş kuzeyi ve batısı' (Avrethisar) and 'Kozana güneyi – Aliakmon Rum köyleri' (Kozana). Aynaroz is taken as 6,640 monks (male-only, not doubled) with 0.9% Muslim officials. There are now 142 clusters, each with population, vilayet, sancak and '[kaza ...]' in groups; the populations of each kaza sum to its estimated total.
Populations: every cluster now has a 1876 population (region total 1,972,110). Selanik vilayeti 981,544, Manastır part 553,094, Prizren part 437,472, matching the vilayet_stats estimate rows.
